channel.title: System Design Revision
channel.description: Long-form audio revision for senior and staff system design interviews: requirements, back-of-envelope numbers, deep dives, curveballs and trade-offs, one canonical design per episode.
channel.itunes:author: Quorum Notes

item.title: News / Discover feed ranking
item.description: A two-voice system design revision: a host explains and a curious learner attempts the recall questions first. It opens with the one-sentence framing and the read API, then the objective (satisfied engagement, not clicks) and the sizing by counting zeros. After the high-level design (pull-based, two-stage funnel) it sweeps seven areas out loud with the mnemonic 'Do We Cache For Speed? Sure, Trade-offs.' before going deep. The deep dives cover five candidate sources and the deadline mixer, story clustering with SimHash and the pigeonhole trick, features and the training-serving skew guard, multi-task ranking with a value formula, calibration and position bias, MMR re-ranking worked through, exploration and propensities, evaluation and safe change, then scaling, failure modes and curveballs, trade-offs, a lightning round and a one-minute arc across the sweep. 13 chapters.

item.title: Distributed cache
item.description: A two-voice system design revision: a host explains and a curious learner asks why, with recall pauses. It opens with a one-sentence framing and the read API, then does the sizing by counting zeros (500 nodes, 20k ops per node, bits to bytes). After the high-level design it sweeps seven areas out loud before going deep: data structures, the write path, the consistency promise, failure modes, safe change, numbers and trade-offs. The deep dives cover fixed hash slots versus mod N and consistent hashing, hash tags, slot migration with ASK and MOVED, delete-on-write and the stale-set race fixed by leases, CDC-driven invalidation, sampled LRU, LFU and W-TinyLFU, majority failover with epochs and fencing, hot keys, XFetch stampede protection, cold starts, curveballs, trade-offs and a one-minute arc. 12 chapters.

item.title: Networking fundamentals: IP addresses, CIDR and prefix matching
item.description: A two-voice explainer. A host explains and a curious newcomer asks why, with recall pauses where you answer before the host does. It covers why an IP address is really one 32-bit number, then CIDR blocks and how much a slash 32, 24, 16, 8 or 0 holds. Next comes the membership test (AND with the netmask), the octet shortcut, and non-aligned prefixes like a slash 20 or slash 23. It goes through the private, CGNAT and loopback ranges and why banning CGNAT causes collateral damage, then longest prefix match for allow-exceptions. On the storage side, it shows how a binary or Patricia trie stores prefixes, why a hash set can't, and sorted intervals with binary search as the alternative. It explains why IPv6 bans target a slash 64, then where all of this shows up in system design rounds, and ends with a lightning round and a one-minute recap. 10 chapters.

item.title: Ad click aggregation: the 7 recall gaps
item.description: A short revision episode on the seven things a from-memory redraw of the ad-click aggregation design missed: the partition key, the reversed join, when the click-ID registry is written, what closes a window, why the sink is an upsert, the missing boxes, and the rollup shape.

item.title: Ad click aggregation, exactly-once
item.description: Exactly-once counting for money in an ad click and impression pipeline. It opens with three consumers (billing, pacing, trending), the numbers, and the campaign, ad, impression and click IDs, then the high-level design. The deep dives cover deduplication with keyed state; event time, watermarks, late data and watermark stalls from idle or slow partitions; the click-to-impression join with its RocksDB impression buffer; what emit means; a consensus-backed click ID registry and why it needs Paxos or Raft; registry expiry and its trap; RocksDB checkpoints with Kafka offsets; the four ingredients of effectively-once and the idempotent sink; the three rollup tables and why click-through rate is derived, never stored; columnar versioned serving and pacing; and the raw archive with nightly reconciliation. It closes with trending, scaling, curveballs, trade-offs and a one-minute recall arc. 17 chapters.

item.title: Top-K ad recommendations
item.description: Ranking-led system design revision: disambiguating top-K, the numbers and latency budget, retrieval (targeting index + two-tower), calibrated click prediction, the second-price auction worked through, pacing and frequency caps, the click-aggregation feedback loop (dedup, join, watermarks, effectively-once), trending top-K, curveballs, trade-offs, and a one-minute arc. 12 chapters.

item.title: Distributed denylist
item.description: System design revision: blocking banned IPs, users and API keys globally at the edge. Requirements and the two asymmetries, high-level design, Bloom filters step by step, the two-tier check and deletes, CIDR ranges and the trie walk, propagation and ordering, consistency and safe change management, scaling, curveballs, trade-offs, and a one-minute arc. 10 chapters.
